first.rationale: Onboarding simplification is the strongest single intervention for the two concurrent funnel declines: prior evidence links reduced friction to both higher onboarding completion and durable first-week activation. Verify both records to confirm segment fit, effect durability, and downstream qualified-revenue measures before committing. Promotional pricing addresses competitive pressure but carries greater uncertainty around customer quality and long-term revenue.

mid.rationale: Run a targeted onboarding-simplification experiment for self-serve SMB accounts. The verified evidence directly addresses both current declines: signup simplification increased activation 9% and qualified revenue 4%, while shortened onboarding increased completion 13%, accelerated time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention 3%. Keep the test bounded because signup simplification showed a 1% retention decline and its result was only confirmed for SMBs; monitor qualified revenue and retention as guardrails.

final2.rationale: Pivot this cycle's experiment to targeted promotional pricing for price-sensitive SMB accounts. The competitor's deeper price cut and doubled price-related churn conversations create an immediate qualified-revenue retention threat, while inherited evidence indicates targeted pricing can lift SMB acquisition and revenue. Use a guarded test rather than a broad rollout because memory_73 could not be source-verified this cycle and discounting may reduce margins, cannibalize full-price revenue, or attract lower-quality accounts. Track qualified revenue, retention, gross margin, and post-promotion conversion as guardrails.
